## How to start

1. Click on a **Open in Colab** badge below (a free Google account is needed).
2. In Colab: *Runtime → Run all*. In the accelerator track, the first cell installs Cheetah (~30 s);
   the nuclear-energy track needs no installation.
3. Fill in the cells marked **✏️ Exercise** (look for `...` and `# TODO`).
4. Stuck? Open the solution notebook.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Save your work
Colab notebooks opened from GitHub are temporary. Use *File → Save a copy in Drive* to keep your answers.
:::

Suggested order: 0 → 1 → 2 → 3. Each notebook takes 30–45 min; notebook 0 is needed for

## Nuclear-energy track

The same methods applied to reactor physics, radiation protection and dosimetry. Each notebook
contains its own small physics simulator; see [ML for nuclear energy](nuclear.qmd) for the
context and references.

| # | Topic | You will learn | Exercise | Solution |
|:-:|:--|:--|:-:|:-:|
| 4 | Radionuclide identification in gamma spectra | simulated NaI spectra; ROI method vs. neural network vs. full-spectrum fit; counting statistics; gain drift and data augmentation; unknown nuclides | [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/hayg25/ML4Accelerators/blob/main/notebooks/04_gamma_spectroscopy.ipynb) | [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/hayg25/ML4Accelerators/blob/main/notebooks/solutions/04_gamma_spectroscopy.ipynb) |
| 5 | Surrogate of a reactor-physics code | Latin-hypercube design; Gaussian process with uncertainty; critical boron search; uncertainty propagation; GP vs. neural network with 40 runs; active learning | [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/hayg25/ML4Accelerators/blob/main/notebooks/05_reactor_surrogate.ipynb) | [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/hayg25/ML4Accelerators/blob/main/notebooks/solutions/05_reactor_surrogate.ipynb) |
| 6 | Neutron/gamma pulse-shape discrimination | pulse simulation; optimised charge comparison; neural network on waveforms; pile-up; gamma rejection at the operating point | [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/hayg25/ML4Accelerators/blob/main/notebooks/06_neutron_gamma_psd.ipynb) | [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/hayg25/ML4Accelerators/blob/main/notebooks/solutions/06_neutron_gamma_psd.ipynb) |

Each nuclear notebook takes 45–60 min and can be done independently of the others.

## Run locally instead

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hayg25/ML4Accelerators.git
cd ML4Accelerators
pip install -r requirements.txt
jupyter lab notebooks/
```
